NEW PATIENT VISIT

CC: Establishing care. Previous doctor retired; records requested.

HPI: 64M with type 2 diabetes for about six years by his count, hypertension since his early fifties, and high cholesterol. Feels fine. Takes metformin 1000 twice a day, lisinopril 20 and amlodipine 5 every morning, and a baby aspirin. Says his sugars "run a little high" and his pressure was always a sore subject with the old office. No home cuff. No chest pain, dyspnea, edema, claudication. No polyuria. No vision change. Bowels regular, no bleeding.

PMH: T2DM. HTN. Hyperlipidemia, never on a statin per patient.
PSH: Tonsillectomy as a boy (about age 8). Knee scope around 2008 (age 55).
Meds: as above.
Allergies: none known.
FH: Father - colon cancer at 70, has since died. Mother - diabetes and high blood pressure.
SH: Retired from the postal service after a long career carrying mail. Married, lives with his wife in Westfield. Never smoked. Does not drink. Walks the neighborhood most mornings.

ROS: 12-point negative except as in HPI.

Exam: Well appearing, pleasant. BP repeated at end of visit, still above goal. HEENT unremarkable. Neck without bruit or thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmur or gallop appreciated. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses or organomegaly. Extremities warm, no edema. Feet: skin intact, monofilament intact bilaterally, DP pulses 2+.

A/P:
1. Type 2 diabetes - A1c, CMP, urine microalbumin today. Continue metformin 1000 BID. Diet review.
2. Hypertension - above goal on lisinopril 20 + amlodipine 5. Not changing today on a first visit; would like home numbers. Bring cuff readings next time.
3. Hyperlipidemia - lipid panel today.
4. Health maintenance - never had a colonoscopy. With his father's history this is overdue; explained why. He would like to think about it and talk to his wife. Hep C and HIV screening offered and done today. Flu shot and pneumonia vaccine next month at a nurse visit.

RTC 3 months, sooner for results.

PCP

documents.title: Cardiology Consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CARDIOLOGY GROUP - CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 03/18/2019
Re: Carl Clark, DOB 09/28/1952
Referred by: primary care

Dear colleague,

Thank you for asking us to see Mr. Clark, a 66-year-old retired letter carrier, for several months of tiredness and a falling-off in how far and how fast he can walk.

He has diabetes and hypertension, the latter never well controlled by his account, along with hyperlipidemia. He takes lisinopril, metformin and amlodipine, plus aspirin 81 mg. No known drug allergies. Never smoker, no alcohol. His father had colon cancer at 70 and is deceased; his mother had diabetes and high blood pressure. Surgical history is a tonsillectomy in childhood and a knee arthroscopy at 55.

Exam: BP 160/96. Pulse 72 and regular. The apical impulse is displaced laterally and there is an S4. I hear no murmur. JVP is not raised, the lungs are clear and there is no peripheral edema; no evidence of heart failure.

Recent labs from your office show normal renal function and electrolytes.

ECG today: sinus rhythm, 72, with voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy.

Impression: Left ventricular hypertrophy, almost certainly the product of years of inadequately treated hypertension. I suspect the pressure load explains much of his reduced exercise tolerance.

Recommendations:
1. Transthoracic echocardiogram to characterize the hypertrophy and LV function; scheduled for 03/28.
2. Tighter BP control is the priority. I would increase amlodipine to 10 mg daily and aim for under 130/80. I will leave the adjustment with you.
3. Continue aspirin.

We would be glad to see him again as needed.

Cardiology
Allergies: NKDA

reports.text:
Complete 2D, M-mode and Doppler study. Technically adequate.
Left ventricle: normal cavity size. Concentric left ventricular hypertrophy; interventricular septum 1.3 cm and posterior wall 1.3 cm in diastole. Normal wall motion. LVEF 60% (biplane).
Right ventricle: normal size and function.
Atria: normal size.
Valves: aortic, mitral, tricuspid and pulmonic valves structurally normal without significant stenosis or regurgitation.
Aorta: normal root dimension.
Pericardium: no effusion.
IVC normal with normal respiratory variation.
reports.conclusion: Concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with normal LV size and systolic function, LVEF 60%. Normal valves. No pericardial effusion.

OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY - NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Date of service: 11/12/2024
Patient: Carl Clark   DOB: 09/28/1952
Referring: primary care (urgent)

Reason: fatigue, weight loss, abnormal liver tests.

History: 72-year-old man with type 2 diabetes, hypertension and hyperlipidemia, seen by cardiology in 2019, who describes four months of steadily worsening fatigue with unplanned weight loss. He gets full quickly, has a mild discomfort in the right upper quadrant and his bowels have become intermittently constipated. He has not had nausea or vomiting and has not seen blood in the stool. He has never had hepatitis or any liver disease that he knows of. He has never had a colonoscopy or any other cancer screening. He does not smoke or drink and takes nothing hepatotoxic.

Medications (per patient list): metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: father with colon cancer at 70, deceased. Mother with diabetes and hypertension.

Examination: Thin man, comfortable. No scleral icterus. Abdomen soft. A firm liver edge is felt 3 cm below the right costal margin; it is not tender. No ascites by exam.

Labs today: AST 51, ALT 44, alkaline phosphatase 189, total bilirubin 1.4, albumin 3.4, INR 1.1. AFP within normal limits.

CT abdomen with IV contrast (done today): multiple liver lesions in both lobes, the largest 4.6 cm, and irregular thickening of the ascending colon wall. Report attached.

Impression: Colorectal neoplasia, likely arising in the ascending colon, with liver lesions that are highly suspicious for metastatic disease.

Plan:
1. Colonoscopy with biopsy - booked 11/21.
2. Image-guided core biopsy of a representative liver lesion through interventional radiology.
3. Oncology referral once tissue is in hand.
4. I discussed these findings frankly with Mr. Clark and his wife.

Thank you for this referral.

documents.title: Operative Report - Right Hemicolectomy
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
OPERATIVE REPORT
Date of surgery: 03/05/2025
Patient: Carl Clark, 72 M

Preoperative diagnosis: adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon with liver metastases; Clostridium septicum bacteremia, treated.
Postoperative diagnosis: same.
Procedure: open right hemicolectomy with primary ileocolic anastomosis.
Anesthesia: general endotracheal.

Indications: biopsy-proven ascending colon cancer, planned for resection of the primary, now admitted with C. septicum bacteremia from the tumor. After four days of IV antibiotics with defervescence and negative repeat cultures, resection was brought forward to this admission.

Findings: mass in the ascending colon, tattooed. Liver with known lesions, not addressed. No peritoneal deposits seen. No perforation.

Description: midline laparotomy. Right colon mobilized along the white line of Toldt; ileocolic pedicle ligated at its origin. Terminal ileum and transverse colon divided with staplers; stapled side-to-side ileocolic anastomosis, common enterotomy closed. Hemostasis. Fascia closed with running looped suture; skin stapled.

Intraoperative events: new atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response during mobilization, treated by anesthesia with IV metoprolol; hemodynamically stable throughout.

EBL 150 mL. Specimen to pathology. Disposition: PACU, then medical floor, stable.

General Surgery

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 03/01/2025 (via ED)   Discharged: 03/14/2025
Service: General Surgery, with hospital medicine co-management
PCP: primary care (copy sent)

Principal diagnosis: sepsis due to Clostridium septicum bacteremia, source colon adenocarcinoma.
Other diagnoses this admission: adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon with liver metastases, s/p open right hemicolectomy 3/5; postoperative atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, resolved; postoperative ileus, resolved; type 2 diabetes; hypertension; hyperlipidemia.

Hospital course:
1. Sepsis / C. septicum bacteremia. Presented febrile, hypotensive and confused. Fluids and piperacillin-tazobactam plus vancomycin; cultures grew gram-positive rods on 3/3, identified as C. septicum; vancomycin stopped. Repeat cultures 3/4 no growth. Mental status back to baseline by 3/3. Completing therapy with oral amoxicillin-clavulanate through 3/21.

2. Colon cancer. Taken for open right hemicolectomy on 3/5 (see operative report). Pathology: moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma, pT3 pN1b, margins negative. Outpatient oncology to resume care and discuss chemotherapy.

3. Postoperative atrial fibrillation with RVR. AF began intraoperatively and was treated with IV metoprolol. He was asymptomatic overnight in normal rhythm by vitals (HR 78, BP 130/85). On the morning of POD 1 (3/6) he reported palpitations and mild shortness of breath; pulse irregularly irregular, BP 120/80; ECG atrial fibrillation, ventricular rate 110. Oral metoprolol tartrate for rate control. Converted to sinus rhythm 3/7 and remained in sinus on telemetry for the rest of the stay. Metoprolol was not continued at discharge.

4. Postoperative ileus. On POD 4 (3/9) abdominal distension with no flatus or stool since surgery; afebrile (37.2), BP 135/85, HR 88; abdomen distended and tympanic, nontender, bowel sounds sparse. Hgb 12.5, WBC 9.0, Na 140, K 4.2, Cl 102, HCO3 24, BUN 18, Cr 1.0. Abdominal films: diffuse bowel gas, no free air. Managed with bowel rest, NG decompression, IV fluids, ambulation and minimal opioids. Flatus POD 6, stool POD 7; NG removed and diet advanced, tolerating a regular diet at discharge.

5. Diabetes - insulin sliding scale plus metformin. HTN - lisinopril continued. Enoxaparin for VTE prophylaxis while inpatient.

Discharge medications:
- Metformin 1000 mg twice daily
- Lisinopril 20 mg daily
- Aspirin 81 mg daily
- Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg twice daily through 3/21 (NEW)

Allergies: NKDA.
Condition at discharge: stable, ambulating independently. Incision clean, staples to come out at the surgical follow-up.
Follow-up: surgery clinic 1-2 weeks; oncology; PCP within 1 week.

CARDIAC CATHETERIZATION LABORATORY
Date: 03/09/2026
Patient: Carl Clark, 73 M
Indication: NSTEMI.
Access: right radial artery, 6 Fr. Hemostasis with radial band.

Coronary angiography:
- Left main: no significant disease.
- LAD: 90% stenosis of the proximal segment. Distal vessel without significant disease.
- Left circumflex: 30% stenosis.
- RCA: 40% stenosis. Dominant.

Intervention: proximal LAD treated with one drug-eluting stent after predilation. 0% residual stenosis, TIMI 3 flow.

Conclusion: single-vessel culprit disease of the proximal LAD, treated with one DES. Nonobstructive disease of the circumflex and RCA.
Recommendations: aspirin indefinitely, clopidogrel for 12 months, high-intensity statin.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 03/07/2026 via ED   Discharged 03/12/2026
Service: Cardiology

Diagnoses: Acute non-ST elevation myocardial infarction with acute pulmonary edema. Coronary artery disease, s/p DES to proximal LAD 3/9. Left ventricular hypertrophy. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension. Hyperlipidemia. Stage IV colon adenocarcinoma with liver metastases.

Course: Presented with 2 hours of substernal pressure and dyspnea, hypoxemic to 88%, BP 100/78, with pulmonary edema on exam and chest film. ECG with ST depression V3-V6; hs-troponin I 1,850 rising to a peak of 16,400 ng/L; NT-proBNP 4,820. Treated with BiPAP, IV furosemide, aspirin and heparin; off BiPAP within 24 hours and on room air by 3/8. Angiography 3/9 via the radial artery: proximal LAD 90% treated with one drug-eluting stent; circumflex 30%, RCA 40%. Echo 3/9: concentric LVH, anterior hypokinesis, LVEF 50%, normal valves. Lisinopril held for the first day for soft pressures and then resumed. Metformin held around contrast and resumed 48 hours afterward. No arrhythmia on telemetry.

Oncology (inpatient consult): maintenance 5-FU/leucovorin to be held; outpatient oncology follow-up to decide next steps.

- Aspirin 81 mg daily (continue)
- Clopidogrel 75 mg daily x 12 months (NEW)

- Metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily (NEW)
- Lisinopril 20 mg daily (continue)
